# Jubilees Chapter 31 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob's reunion with Isaac; the blessings of Levi and Judah

---

**31:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, second week, second year, Jacob came home to his parents at Mamre — the valley near Hebron.

**31:2** He settled in his father's house at Mamre, keeping Rachel and Leah, his servants, all his children, and all his flocks close by.

**31:3** On the first day of the seventh month, Isaac held a feast. He sent for Jacob, who came and brought his father a gift.

**31:4** Jacob hesitated at the doorway — his father was old and blind. But Rebekah pushed him: "Don't be afraid. Go to him."

**31:5** Jacob stepped in. Isaac reached out, pulled him close, and wept over him, kissing his face. "My son — my eyes are gone and I can't see you, but I know your smell and your voice."

**31:6** "It's Jacob, Father," he said. "Your son who loves you."

**31:7** "Why have you come?" Isaac asked. "To see you," Jacob said. "To kiss your hands. To be blessed. To have you pray for me."

**31:8** Isaac held him, embraced him, and cried.

**31:9** Then Isaac called for Levi. "Come here, son." Levi came forward and Isaac laid his right hand on Levi's head and his left on his shoulder.

**31:10** "May the God of all — the LORD of all ages — bless you and your sons forever, generation after generation. May God make you and your descendants a priestly nation, the holiest of all peoples, for all time.

**31:11** May the fullness of priesthood be yours and your sons' and your grandsons'. May you stand holy and great before God, your family exalted and honored in his presence.

**31:12** Serve in God's sanctuary — be blessed and set apart. Be a prince among the sons of God. May all peoples fall under your authority, and may your children's children be holy.

**31:13** He has singled you out from among all humanity to serve him — to stand in his sanctuary, to minister before him, and to be a channel of blessing for all the earth."

**31:14** Levi stepped back. Then Isaac called Judah forward and placed his right hand on Judah's head.

**31:15** "May the LORD God of all bless you forever, my son. May he make you mighty for victory over every nation. May the peoples who don't know you tremble at your name. May every king on earth stand in awe of you.

**31:16** May your harvest be rich and your family grow great. May your dominion spread across the earth. Rise high, my son — build strength into your line.

**31:17** Be king and prince over all peoples. May every nation bow before you."

**31:18** He put both hands on Judah's head and kissed him: "May the LORD God bless you — the Holy God of Israel, sovereign over all the earth. May he make you holy and choose your people."

**31:19** Jacob was overjoyed. He praised God, then threw himself face-down before his father and bowed.

**31:20** At that moment the spirit of prophecy fell on Isaac and he spoke: "Blessed are you, LORD God of Israel — you have kept me and my fathers' generations, those who never broke your covenant. You have blessed Jacob, and through Jacob you have blessed Levi and Judah."

**31:21** When Isaac stood up and saw all twelve of Jacob's sons standing there, he wept with joy and blessed every one of them.

**31:22** Jacob left his father's house that day with a full heart, and ran to tell his mother the good news.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Isaac's separate blessings for Levi (priestly) and Judah (royal) are programmatic in Jubilees, establishing the two-office model. The spirit of prophecy on Isaac (v.20) frames the entire blessing scene as divinely inspired. This is a uniquely expanded scene not found in Genesis.*
